title: Capacity Laddering with Grace Windows: pricing schematic for reserved + burst
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a differentiated Dedicated capacity offering that balances procurement simplicity with operational elasticity. Proposal introduces a 'laddered commitment' pricing model plus a 72-hour 'grace window' buffer that allows limited bursts above committed GPU capacity at softened overage rates before autoscale or strict throttling kicks in. This ticket drives the experiment design, financial simulation, contract language (SQ implications), and pilot plan.

Scope:
- Pricing ladder: 3 committed bands (Base, Growth, Peak) with increasing volume discounts and pre-set burst credit allowances.
- Grace window: transient buffer (configurable 24/72/168h) where customers can exceed their committed capacity for short periods without immediate contract penalties; usage during grace is billed at a mid-tier overage rate and consumes burst credits.
- Autoscale interaction: define when autoscale (metered on-demand capacity) should activate vs. consuming grace/burst credits.
- SLA tiers mapping: Bronze/Silver/Gold with defined latency SLOs, guaranteed burst availability % (probabilistic), and financial remedies.
- Contract & SQ: update term-sheet pricing clauses, add required SQ responses for burst capacity controls, and confirm KMS/HSM language and audit logging expectations.

Constraints & Risks:
- Complexity: Too many configurable knobs will slow procurement; target 2-3 knobs surfaced in sales-facing docs.
- Financial risk: Grace windows open us to short-term cost spikes; simulations need worst-case tails and mitigation (per-customer caps + auto-billing thresholds).
- Operational: Orchestration must be able to enforce burst credit accounting and map to Dedicated pools; requires infra work (ENG) and observability (console + billing).

Success metrics:
- Conversion: +15% conversion from POC to committed capacity in pilot accounts vs baseline.
- Revenue: >5% uplift in ARR for participants due to smoother commit upsell.
- Ops: <2 incidents caused by burst handling in first 90 days.

Deliverables:
- Pricing schematic + econ model (spreadsheet link in comments).
- Redlined contract language for Sales & Legal.
- Console mock for toggling grace window & ladder bands.
- Pilot plan with 2 enterprise customers and measurement plan.
acceptance_criteria: Econ model completed and stress-tested: baseline, 95th percentile, and worst-case tails documented

Implementation backlog stories created for ENG with clear owners and SLAs for burst accounting
